```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(zoo)
library(arrow)
library(scales)
library(lubridate)
library(ggrepel)
library(ggbeeswarm)

# ==========================================
# GOOGLE TRENDS DATA PREP
# ==========================================
all_df <- read_csv("data/clean/clean_time_series_US_5.csv")

# Convert to tidy format and rename
tidy_df <- all_df |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(matcha, matcha_latte, strawberry_ml, boba, psl),
    names_to = "keyword",
    values_to = "interest"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    keyword = recode(
      keyword,
      matcha = "Matcha",
      matcha_latte = "Matcha Latte",
      strawberry_ml = "Strawberry Matcha Latte",
      boba = "Boba",
      psl = "Pumpkin Spice Latte"
    )
  )

# Calculate growth stats since 2021
growth_stats <- tidy_df |>
  filter(time >= as.Date("2021-01-01")) |>
  group_by(keyword) |>
  summarise(
    start = first(interest),
    end = last(interest),
    pct_growth = ((end - start) / start) * 100
  )

# Calculate standard deviation since 2021
std <- tidy_df |>
  filter(time >= as.Date("2021-01-01")) |>
  group_by(keyword) |>
  summarize(
    mean_interest = mean(interest),
    sd_interest = sd(interest),
    cv = sd_interest / mean_interest
  )

# Filter for recent trends
trends_recent <- tidy_df |>
  filter(time >= as.Date("2016-01-01"), keyword != "Strawberry Matcha Latte")

trends_recent_1 <- tidy_df |>
  filter(time >= as.Date("2021-01-01"), keyword != "Strawberry Matcha Latte")

# Rolling Average Dataframe
rol_avg <- trends_recent |>
  group_by(keyword) |>
  arrange(time) |>
  mutate(rolling_avg = rollmean(interest, k = 6, fill = NA))

# Second Rolling Average Dataframe
rol_avg_1 <- trends_recent_1 |>
  group_by(keyword) |>
  arrange(time) |>
  mutate(rolling_avg = rollmean(interest, k = 3, fill = NA))

# Get the peak month for matcha rolling average 
peak_matcha <- rol_avg_1 |> 
  filter(keyword == "Matcha") |> 
  arrange(desc(rolling_avg)) |> 
  slice(1)

# Matcha Beverages Dataframe 
matcha_beverages <- tidy_df |>
  filter(keyword %in% c("Matcha Latte", "Strawberry Matcha Latte"),
         time >= as.Date("2016-01-01"))

# Monthly Seasonality Dataframe
monthly_avg <- tidy_df |>
  mutate(month = month(time, label = TRUE)) |>
  group_by(keyword, month) |>
  summarise(avg_interest = mean(interest), .groups = 'drop')

# ==========================================
# TIKTOK DATA PREP
# ==========================================
tiktok_data <- read_parquet("data/clean/clean_tiktok_data.parquet")

plot_data <- tiktok_data |>
  mutate(
    caption_lower = tolower(caption),
    category = case_when(
      str_detect(caption_lower, "ceremonial") ~ "Traditional",
      str_detect(caption_lower, "starbucks") ~ "Commercial",
      str_detect(caption_lower, "strawberry") ~ "Flavor Innovation",
      str_detect(caption_lower, "latte") ~ "Cafe Beverage",
      TRUE ~ "General Matcha"
    )
  ) |>
  select(-caption_lower)
```

### Box 2: Matcha Standard Deviation Since 2021
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
matcha_latte_sd <- std |>
  filter(keyword == "Matcha Latte") |>
  pull(sd_interest)

matcha_latte_cv <- std |>
  filter(keyword == "Matcha Latte") |>
  pull(cv)

boba_sd <- std |>
  filter(keyword == "Boba") |>
  pull(sd_interest)

boba_cv <- std |>
  filter(keyword == "Boba") |>
  pull(cv)

cv_comparison <- sprintf("%.1f%% vs %.1f%%", matcha_latte_cv * 100, boba_cv * 100)
```

<div style="font-size: 2.2em; font-weight: bold; text-align: center; padding: 5px; color: #2C3E50;">

Matcha Latte has shown a steady interest since 2021 compared to Boba

## Row {height="42.5%"}

### Rolling Average (6-month period) Line plot
```{r}
ggplot(rol_avg_1, aes(x = time, y = rolling_avg, color = keyword)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  # vertical line for the peak
  geom_vline(xintercept = peak_matcha$time, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray35") +
  # text label pointing to the peak
  geom_label_repel(
    data = peak_matcha,
    aes(label = paste("Peak Market Interest\n", format(time, "%b %Y"))),
    nudge_y = 10,
    nudge_x = -300,
    show.legend = FALSE,
    fontface = "bold",
    color = "black", 
    segment.colour = "black"
  ) + 
  labs(
    title = "6-Month Rolling Search Momentum",
    subtitle = "Tracking sustained interest vs. temporary viral spikes (2021-2026)",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Rolling Average Interest"
  ) + 
  theme_minimal() + 
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_blank()
  )
```

## Row {height="42.5%"}

### Monthly Average Seasonal Line Plot
```{r}
ggplot(monthly_avg, aes(x = month, y = avg_interest, color = keyword, group = keyword)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Monthly Search Interest",
    subtitle = "An average of each month from 2016 - 2026",
    x = "Month",
    y = "Average Interest") + 
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14))
```

# Social Intent (TikTok)

## Row {height="50%"}

### Consumer Engagement Patterns: Saves vs Views Scatterplot
```{r}
ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = views, y = saves, color = category)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = label_comma()) + 
  scale_y_log10(labels = label_comma()) +
  # Trend line 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, linewidth = 1) + 
  labs(
    title = "Consumer Engagement Patterns: Saves vs Views",
    subtitle = "Comparing engagement across distinct consumer personas (Commercial vs. Traditional)",
    x = "Total Views (Log Scale)",
    y = "Total Saves (Log Scale)",
    color = "Market Segment"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14))
```

## Row {height="50%"}

### Engagement Rate by Category Beeswarm Plot
```{r}
ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = reorder(category, engagement_rate, FUN = median), 
                      y = engagement_rate, 
                      color = category)) +
  geom_quasirandom(alpha = 0.6, size = 2.5, width = 0.2) +
  # Black point to show median
  stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "point", shape = 15, size = 3, color = "black") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_percent()) + 
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 0.3)) + 
  labs(
    title = "Engagement Rate Distribution by Matcha Content Segment",
    subtitle = "Black square indicates the median engagement rate. Each dot is a video.\nEngagement is calculated by (Likes+Comments+Shares+Saves / Views)",
    x = "Market Segment",
    y = "Engagement Rate"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold")
  )
```
